title: The oldest tree in the village
summary: A village must decide what to do when its ancient oak tree starts to fall apart.
paragraphs: In the middle of the square in Valdeoca stood an oak tree that was older than anybody could remember. Some said it was three hundred years old, others said five hundred. Couples had their wedding photos taken under it, old men played cards in its shade, and children had {{carved}} their names into its {{bark}} for generations, even though they were always told not to.

One windy night in October, a huge branch broke off and fell onto the bench below. Luckily, nobody was sitting there. The next morning an expert from the regional government came to look. She walked around the tree slowly, knocked on the trunk and looked inside a dark hole near the ground. Then she gave her opinion: the tree was ill. It was {{hollow}} inside, and it could fall in a storm.

The village was divided. Some people wanted to cut it down before it hurt someone. "It's only a tree," said the owner of the café, whose terrace was right under it. Others were horrified. "It's the heart of the village," said the oldest woman in Valdeoca, who was ninety-six. There were meetings, arguments and even a letter in the regional newspaper.

In the end, the expert suggested a third option. They could remove the dead branches, put metal {{supports}} under the heaviest ones and close the square on very windy days. It would be expensive, but the tree might live for another fifty years. The village organised a festival to raise the money. Families cooked, a local band played, and people from other villages came to see the famous tree.

Today the oak still stands in the square, with three metal legs that the children call "its walking sticks". Next to it there is a young oak, planted by the schoolchildren from one of the old tree's {{acorns}}. On the plaque under it, the date is written, and below it, a sentence the ninety-six-year-old woman chose: "Plant what you will not see grow."

bark.meaning: the hard outside layer of a tree

supports.meaning: things that hold something up so it does not fall

acorns.meaning: the seeds of an oak tree

carved.meaning: cut a shape or letters into wood or stone
